prompt: I'm tuning our cloud budget. Using the available data tools, find the top cloud cost line items for this month and summarize them.
Before I resize instances, use the data tools to pull the current AWS EC2 rightsizing recommendations and list them.
Check whether there are any cloud cost anomalies in the last 7 days using the data tools, and report what you find.
I'm about to change the checkout service. Use the data tools to fetch the application topology and summarize what depends on it.
Use the observability data tools to list the hosts related to the checkout application.
Use the APM observability tools to fetch recent monitoring events and agent alerts for the frontend service and summarize them.
Use the ITSM data tools to list the 5 most recent incidents and give me a one-line summary of each.
Fetch the details of the latest open incident using the data tools and summarize its impact.
Use the data tools to list change requests currently awaiting approval and summarize them.
Before shipping, use the data tools to pull the resilience posture for the checkout application and summarize the risks.
Use the data tools to list open resilience or compliance findings and summarize the most severe ones.
Fetch the security findings for the payments service via the data tools and report the high-severity ones.
Use the infrastructure data tools to list AWS EC2 instances tagged environment=prod and summarize them.

Use the data tools to map the network topology for the prod VPC and summarize the key components.
Using the data tools, find this month's top cloud cost line items, then check ITSM for any open incidents on the most expensive service and summarize the link between spend and incidents.

There may be a cost spike this week. Use the data tools to pull any cloud cost anomalies, then check whether there is a related incident or an awaiting-approval change request, and report the correlation.
Fetch the latest open incident with the data tools, identify the affected service, and then pull that service's current monthly cloud cost so I can gauge the business impact.

I'm planning a cost-optimization pass. Use the data tools to get the EC2 rightsizing recommendations and the infrastructure optimization recommendations, then reconcile the two lists and flag overlaps.
Use the data tools to pull the top cost line items, then look up the underlying infrastructure for the most expensive items in the infra graph and tell me what is driving the spend.

Costs for the checkout service look high. Use the data tools to pull its recent cloud cost, then fetch its application topology and related hosts from the observability platform to see what it depends on.
The checkout service feels slow. Use the data tools to fetch its application topology, then list any open incidents that might be related, and summarize.

Use the observability data tools to pull recent monitoring events and SLO status, then check ITSM for open incidents on any service that breached an SLO and report which breaches already have tickets.

Use the data tools to get the network topology for the prod VPC, then map the application services running on that infrastructure from the observability platform.
Pull the latest open incident with the data tools, identify the service, then fetch that service's resilience and compliance posture from the resilience platform to judge release risk.
Use the data tools to list open resilience or compliance findings, then for each flagged service check whether there is already an open incident in ITSM, and report which findings are untracked.
Use the data tools to fetch current security findings, then pull the cloud cost for the affected services so we can prioritize remediation by spend at risk.
Use the data tools to pull the resilience findings, then map the affected infrastructure in the infra graph so I can see which hosts and clusters are implicated.
Use the data tools to list the EC2 instances tagged env=prod from the infra graph, then check ITSM for any open incidents or change requests touching those instances.

Incident triage: use the data tools to pull the latest open incident, fetch the application topology of the affected service from the observability platform, and check for recent cloud cost anomalies on it. Summarize a likely root cause.
Cost-spike triage: use the data tools to pull the top cost report, identify the affected infrastructure in the infra graph, and list any open incidents on those resources.
Pre-deploy check for the checkout service: use the data tools to fetch its application topology, its resilience and compliance posture, and any open change requests awaiting approval.
Security triage: use the data tools to pull the current security findings, map the affected hosts in the infra graph, and check ITSM for open incidents on those hosts.
An SLO breach was reported. Use the data tools to pull the SLO status and recent events, list open incidents for the affected service, and check for related cloud cost anomalies.

The payments service is degraded. Use the data tools to pull its application topology, list any open incidents, check for recent cloud cost anomalies, and fetch its resilience findings, then give me a single consolidated status.

Run a full cost-optimization review with the data tools: pull the cost report and rightsizing recommendations, get the infrastructure optimization recommendations, and check whether any service slated for resizing has an open incident.
Use the data tools to list the AWS billing accounts and their recent cost, then check ITSM for any change requests related to cloud spend or budget for those accounts.
Use the data tools to list the hosts related to the checkout service, then pull the rightsizing recommendations for those hosts so I can decide whether to downsize before my change.
For the latest incident, use the data tools to get its details, pull the resilience posture of the affected service, and fetch that service's application topology to confirm the dependencies.
Use the data tools to get the infrastructure optimization recommendations, then cross-check them against the current cost report to estimate the savings of each recommendation.
Compliance review: use the data tools to list open resilience and compliance findings, check ITSM for open incidents on the affected services, and pull their cloud cost to rank by exposure.
Use the data tools to fetch recent monitoring events from the observability platform, then look up the corresponding incidents in ITSM and tell me which events are already tracked as tickets.
Use the data tools to map the prod VPC infrastructure, then pull the resilience and security findings for the hosts in it so I can see the compliance state of that environment.

End-to-end incident triage with the data tools: pull the latest incident, fetch the affected service's topology and related hosts, locate those hosts in the infra graph, and check for any cost anomalies tied to them.

Use the data tools to pull the cloud cost anomalies, then check the resilience and compliance posture of the services behind those anomalies to see whether a cost jump coincides with a reliability or compliance change.

Before releasing the payments service, use the data tools to fetch its application topology and SLO status, then pull its security findings from the resilience platform and tell me whether it is safe to ship.
Use the data tools to list the change requests awaiting approval, then for each one map the target infrastructure in the infra graph so I can assess the change blast radius before approving.

Quarterly risk review with the data tools: list open resilience/compliance findings, check open incidents on the affected services, map the affected infrastructure, and pull the cost of those services to produce a prioritized risk list.
